subtitle: Songs Without Script: The Kingri That Remembers

panels.shot: low-angle, twilight wide of a lone bard on a Gond hilltop, kingri raised against a star-scattered sky
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana stands on a rocky rise above dark sal forests, eyes closed, kingri poised mid-stroke, as faint village fires glow in the valley like scattered embers of memory.

dialogue.text: In Gondwana, where royal chronicles lie silent, the Pardhan bards sing — can a people’s history live only in the trembling string of a kingri?

i18n.hi: गोंडवाना में जहाँ राज-दास्तानें खामोश हैं, पारधान गाते हैं — क्या किसी कौम की तारीख बस एक थरथराती किंगरी में बच सकती है?

panels.shot: slow push-in on a weathered hand tuning the kingri strings beside a mud house
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sits on a packed-earth veranda at dawn, carefully tightening the gut strings of his kingri while smoke from a kitchen fire curls behind him.

dialogue.text: The written records of Garha-Katanga are few, scattered in Persian and foreign eyes, but in Mandla’s villages the Pardhan’s hand remembers what ink forgot.

i18n.hi: गढ़ा-कटंगा के लिखित रिकॉर्ड कम हैं, फ़ारसी और परदेसियों में बिखरे, पर मांडला के गाँवों में पारधान का हाथ वही याद रखता है जो स्याही भूल गई।

panels.shot: wide village scene, Pardhan walking on a dusty path with kingri slung, children peeking from doorways
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana walks through a Gond hamlet, kingri over his shoulder, as curious children and an old woman watch from low doorways shaded by thatched roofs.

dialogue.text: Ethnographers like Verrier Elwin and Fürer-Haimendorf found them not in palaces, but in dusty lanes — hereditary bards moving from patron to patron with song as their archive.

i18n.hi: वरीयर एल्विन और फ्यूरर‑हाइमेनडॉर्फ जैसे जाति-शोधक उन्हें महलों में नहीं, धूल भरी गलियों में मिले — पुश्तैनी गायक, एक सरदार से दूसरे तक, गीत को ही अपना ख़ज़ाना बना कर।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot, Pardhan seated opposite a Gond patron family in a dim hut
panels.action: Inside a dim, smoky hut, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sits cross-legged before a Gond farmer and his family, the kingri resting on his lap as all lean in, listening.

dialogue.text: He is Pardhan — the appointed one — tied by obligation to his Gond patron, bound to receive grain and gifts, and in return to guard the line of names reaching back to kings and ancestors.

i18n.hi: वह पारधान है — नियुक्त, बँधा अपने गोंड माईक से — बदले में अनाज और भेंट, और उसके बदले राजा और पुरखों की लंबी नस्ल याद रखने की जिम्मेदारी।

panels.shot: close-up on the kingri’s bow drawing across the strings, sparks of a hearth behind
panels.action: The bow of the kingri in the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana’s hand draws across the strings, a faint vibration visible as the hearth behind throws orange light on his fingers.

dialogue.text: No palm-leaf chronicles, no court scribes, yet his kingri carries creation cycles, clan origins, and the rise and fall of Gond rulers in patterns of rhythm and tune.

i18n.hi: न ताड़पत्र, न दरबारी लिपिकार, फिर भी उसकी किंगरी में सृष्टि-कथाएँ, कुल की जड़ें और गोंड राजाओं का उत्थान-पतन लय और धुन में दर्ज है।

panels.shot: evocative montage wide, Pardhan singing before a group, faint overlay of imagined royal processions in the forest haze
panels.action: As the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sings before a semi-circle of Gond men and women, the forest smoke above them seems to shape faint silhouettes of elephants, spears and royal parasols marching.

dialogue.text: His songs speak of a world we know from scattered documents — Garha-Katanga, Mandla, royal courts and campaigns — but the exact verses of Sangram Shah’s day have vanished into time’s haze.

i18n.hi: उसके गीत उस दुनिया की बात करते हैं जिसे हम बिखरे काग़ज़ों से जानते हैं — गढ़ा‑कटंगा, मांडला, दरबार और जंग — पर संग्राम शाह के ज़माने के सटीक बोल अब धुँधले वक़्त में खो गए।

panels.shot: scholarly split-scene: Pardhan performing on one side, a distant ghosted image of a Persian scribe on the other
panels.action: On one side, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana performs before villagers; on the other, faint and distant, a Persian court scribe dips a reed pen into ink over a manuscript.

dialogue.text: While Persian chroniclers listed battles and alliances, Pardhan bards threaded those same rulers into myths of origin and duty, preserving not minutes of court, but memory as the people felt it.

i18n.hi: जब फ़ारसी इतिहासकार बस जंग और संधियाँ गिनते रहे, पारधान गायकों ने उन्हीं राजाओं को जन्म-कथा और फ़र्ज़ की कहानियों में पिरोया, दरबार की कारवाई नहीं, लोगों की याद बचाई।

panels.shot: low, reverent wide inside a simple Gond shrine, Pardhan singing before clan deities
panels.action: In a small shrine marked by stones and wooden posts, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sings with eyes closed before clan deities, as oil lamps flicker and shadows fall on painted motifs.

dialogue.text: Fürer-Haimendorf noted how Pardhans narrated the birth of the earth, the journey of gods, the founding of lineages — their performance was worship, genealogy and political memory woven together.

i18n.hi: फ्यूरर‑हाइमेनडॉर्फ ने लिखा कैसे पारधान धरती की पैदाइश, देवताओं की यात्राएँ, कुलों की नींव सुनाते हैं — उनका गान पूजा, वंशावली और सियासी याद सबको एक साथ बुनता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Pardhan reciting names, villagers counting on fingers, serious faces
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana chants a measured list of ancestor names, while a middle-aged Gond man follows on his fingers, others listening with intent, brows furrowed in concentration.

dialogue.text: In those lists of names lay rights to land, status and ritual. A misremembered ancestor could mean a lost field, a forgotten share — the stakes of memory were as real as tax and grain.

i18n.hi: उन नामों की सूचियों में ज़मीन, इज़्ज़त और रस्मों के हक़ छुपे थे। एक गलती से बोले पुरखा का मतलब हो सकता था एक खेत कम, एक हिस्सा गायब — याद का दाँव भी टैक्स और अनाज जितना सख़्त था।

panels.shot: transition wide shot through time: forest night with Pardhan singing, dissolving into a 20th-century researcher sketching notes
panels.action: A night-time scene shows the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana singing under the stars; the image blends into a bespectacled 20th-century researcher in khadi clothes, scribbling notes by lantern light nearby.

dialogue.text: By the early twentieth century, men like Elwin sat at the edge of these gatherings, taking down fragments, translating, interpreting — saving some verses even as others slipped away unrecorded.

i18n.hi: बीसवीं सदी की शुरुआत तक, एल्विन जैसे लोग इन जमघटों के किनारे बैठ कर टुकड़े लिखते, अनुवाद, तर्जुमा करते रहे — कुछ पंक्तियाँ बचीं, कई बिना लिखे फिसल गईं।

panels.shot: closer on researcher and Pardhan conversing, kingri between them on the ground
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sits facing a notebook-bearing outsider; between them on the ground lies the kingri, as if bridging two worlds, while they speak quietly.

dialogue.speaker: the_pardhan_bards
dialogue.text: You write my song; but will you also carry my hunger?

i18n.hi: तुम मेरा गीत लिखोगे; मेरी भूख भी उठाओगे?

panels.shot: mid-shot of Pardhan returning from a town, modern road in background, plastic bag in hand
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana walks along a tar road, kingri in one hand, a small plastic bag of provisions in the other, as a bus roars past him in a blur.

dialogue.text: As roads cut through the old forests and wage labour pulled Gond patrons away, the steady patronage of Pardhans thinned; some laid the kingri aside, others reshaped their art to survive.

i18n.hi: जब सड़कें जंगल चीरने लगीं और मज़दूरी ने गोंड सरदारों को बाहर खींच लिया, पारधानों की स्थिर सरपरस्ती घटी; कुछ ने किंगरी छोड़ दी, कुछ ने कला को बदल कर जीना सीखा।

panels.shot: interior wide, Pardhan teaching a child the kingri inside a modest house with a radio
panels.action: Inside a modest cement house with a small radio on a shelf, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana guides a young boy’s hands on the kingri, both focused intensely.

dialogue.text: Yet in many homes, elders still trained children in the old tunes, fitting them around school, factory shifts, and the crackling voices of distant cities on the radio.

i18n.hi: फिर भी कई घरों में बूढ़े अब भी बच्चों को पुरानी धुनें सिखाते हैं, स्कूल, कारखाने की ड्यूटी और रेडियो पर दूर शहरों की चटखती आवाज़ों के बीच उन्हें फिट करते हुए।

panels.shot: evocative split-panel style: one half showing a Pardhan singing; the other, a hand painting dots and lines on paper
panels.action: In one half, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sings, eyes uplifted; in the other, a younger hand draws flowing lines and dot patterns of animals and spirits on a sheet of paper.

dialogue.text: From this same storytelling world, artists like Jangarh Singh Shyam emerged in the late twentieth century, shifting songs and myths onto paper and canvas in a new visual language.

i18n.hi: इसी किस्सागो दुनिया से जंघर सिंह श्याम जैसे कलाकार उभरे, जिन्होंने देर बीसवीं सदी में गीतों और मिथकों को काग़ज़ और कैनवास पर नई चित्रभाषा में उतारा।

panels.shot: museum-like wide, modern gallery with Gond paintings, shadowy figure of Pardhan superimposed in reflection
panels.action: A modern art gallery displays bright Gond paintings on white walls; in the glass, the faint reflection of the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana’s profile appears, kingri on his shoulder.

dialogue.text: Scholars like Jyotindra Jain showed how such works were not relics of a frozen ‘tribal’ past, but living, changing expressions — kin to the songs, yet not copies of a sixteenth-century court style.

i18n.hi: ज्योतिन्द्र जैन जैसे विद्वानों ने दिखाया कि ये काम जमे हुए ‘आदिवासी’ अतीत की चीज़ नहीं, बल्कि बदलती ज़िंदा अभिव्यक्तियाँ हैं — गीतों के क़रीबी, पर किसी सोलहवीं सदी के दरबारी अंदाज़ की हूबहू नकल नहीं।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Pardhan’s face lit by firelight, eyes reflecting both flames and a distant electric bulb
panels.action: The Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sits by a small fire at night, his face lined and thoughtful, one eye catching the flame, the other reflecting a distant electric bulb outside.

dialogue.text: The melodies he carries have shifted with time, verses dropped and added; historians cannot lift a perfect script of Sangram Shah’s court from them, but they reveal what rule felt like from below.

i18n.hi: उसकी धुनें वक़्त के साथ बदल गई हैं, बोल जुड़ते‑टूटते रहे; इतिहासकार इनसे संग्राम शाह के दरबार की कोई बिल्कुल सही स्क्रिप्ट नहीं निकाल सकते, पर इनके ज़रिए राज का नीचे से महसूस होना ज़रूर दिखता है।

panels.shot: wide night shot, Pardhan performing at a village gathering under electric bulbs and stars
panels.action: Under a string of bare electric bulbs and a sky full of stars, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana sits on a raised platform, singing to a mixed crowd of elders, youths and children seated on the ground.

dialogue.text: Tonight, as he plays, those listening hear not only gods and kings, but echoes of their own fathers’ labours, mothers’ stories, and the long arc of Gond history folded into song.

i18n.hi: आज रात, जब वह बजाता है, सुनने वाले सिर्फ देवता और राजा नहीं सुनते, बल्कि अपने बापों की मेहनत, माओं की बातें और गोंड तारीख़ की लंबी धार को भी गीत में घुला हुआ पाते हैं।

panels.shot: closing wide, dawn over Mandla river, Pardhan silhouette crossing a shallow ford with kingri
panels.action: At first light over a broad river near Mandla, the Pardhan Bard of Gondwana wades through the shallow ford, his silhouette small against the pale sky, kingri held high above the water.

dialogue.text: As archives and screens multiply, the Pardhan’s kingri reminds us that a people’s past can also live in a voice, a journey, and a promise passed from ear to ear without a single written word.

i18n.hi: जब दस्तावेज़ और स्क्रीनें बढ़ती जा रही हैं, पारधान की किंगरी याद दिलाती है कि किसी कौम का अतीत एक आवाज़, एक सफ़र और कान से कान तक चली एक कसम में भी ज़िंदा रह सकता है, बिना एक भी लिखित शब्द के।

title_i18n.en: Pardhan Bards Keep the Gond Memory
title_i18n.hi: पारधान गायक बचाते हैं गोंडों की याद

subtitle_i18n.en: Songs Without Script: The Kingri That Remembers
subtitle_i18n.hi: बिन लिपि के गीत: याद रखने वाली किंगरी
